# Artifact Keeper 1.10.1

A patch release on the 1.10 line. The headline is a startup fix: **a hex `JWT_SECRET` is no longer refused as low entropy**. Alongside it come three advisory-scanning correctness fixes and one corrected API value. No schema migrations.

## Hex `JWT_SECRET` values work again

Since 1.7.0 the backend has refused to start with `JWT_SECRET is unsuitable: it has low entropy` for about one in four secrets generated with `openssl rand -hex 32`. The check required 16 distinct characters, and hex has exactly 16, so a random 64-character hex secret missed the bar whenever it happened to leave out a digit. That happens about 23% of the time (#4211).

The check now estimates entropy from the character classes the secret uses, at 4 bits per character for hex and 6 for base64, and requires 128 bits. A 64-character hex secret passes, and the shortest hex secret accepted is 32 characters. The 32-character minimum, the placeholder and weak-substring lists and the monotonic-sequence check have not changed.

**If you worked around this**, for example by switching to a base64 secret or by regenerating the hex value until the backend accepted it, you don't need to do anything. Your current secret still works, and hex secrets are accepted again if you want to go back to them. One case is stricter: a secret made of a short string repeated (`abab…`, or the same 16 characters pasted four times) is now judged on a single copy and can be refused even if it passed before. Any secret generated with `openssl rand` is unaffected.

## Fixed — advisory scanning

These three share a root cause. The OSV.dev batch response was flattened into one list instead of being read in query order. All three are present in 1.8.2, 1.9.0 and 1.10.0.

- **A vulnerability in one dependency was cached against every dependency scanned in the same batch**, for the full one-hour cache TTL. A later artifact that only shared one of those dependencies inherited a fabricated finding that looked exactly like a real one (#4079).
- **Findings named the first dependency in the manifest** instead of the one they were about. The wrong name went into generated SBOMs and into the finding dedup key (#4081).
- **An advisory-feed outage was recorded as a clean, complete scan.** Scans that ran while OSV.dev or the GitHub Advisory Database could not answer are now graded `partial` (#4080).

**Expect `partial` scans during feed outages.** This behaviour change is intended and shows up across the whole fleet. The findings themselves don't change and no scan fails, but alerting or gating on `scan_completeness = complete` will now see those scans. A deployment with no GitHub token configured is not affected by this, because skipping the GitHub feed doesn't count as an outage.

## Fixed — repository format strings

**The API now returns format values it accepts back.** `conda_native`, `wasm_oci` and `helm_oci` repositories were served as `condanative`, `wasmoci` and `helmoci`. The UI showed those repositories as `GENERIC`, and sending the value back to the API failed with `400 Invalid format`. **Clients that match on the old spellings must switch to the underscored names** (#4085).

The full entries are in the `## [1.10.1]` section of [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/blob/v1.10.1/CHANGELOG.md).
